_meta.purpose: Box-semantics + comedic-engine library for SLAP's meme templates. For each template in generate_memes.py's CURATED_TEMPLATES this documents WHO the meme is about (subject), WHERE the laugh comes from (engine + comedic_engine), the REQUIRED relationship between caption boxes (valence), and a worked/anti example pair. Replaces the mechanics-only v1.
_meta.consumption_model: Two projections are derived from this file. (1) prompts/meme_selector_index.txt -- a compact one-line-per-template index for PASS 1, which already seeds meme_concept and is the natural place to pick the template slug. (2) The full entry for the 1-2 selected templates only, injected into PASS 2 for caption writing. The whole file is NOT injected wholesale -- at ~30 full entries that is roughly 23k tokens competing with voice_examples.txt for the writer's attention.
_meta.source_of_truth: Imgflip live get_memes API for box_count; uat/meme_box_check.py enforces it at run time.
_meta.status_field: 'status' tracks review state of the SEMANTICS ONLY -- not the template_id. Every entry is 'candidate' (AI-authored, awaiting review). No 'verified' tier exists yet.
_meta.subject_is_mandatory: Every template requires a subject -- the person/team/org the meme is about. subject.placement is either 'box:N' (a caption box names them) or 'copy' (the surrounding prose must). Where placement is 'copy', subject.rule is a HARD requirement: the subject must be named in the sentence immediately before or after the meme, and if no specific subject can be named the template must not be used. ENFORCEMENT GAP: pass2_writer.txt does not currently carry this rule and nothing validates it. See open_questions_for_review.
_meta.engine_axis: 'engine' is the shared comedic mechanism -- templates in one engine share comedic_engine, valence_rule, key_test and failure_mode (defined once under _meta.engines). 'pattern_type' is the separate structural axis: how captions map onto physical panels. Two templates can share an engine but differ in pattern_type (drake vs distracted-boyfriend) or vice versa. The taxonomy is open -- add a new engine rather than force a bad fit.
_meta.examples_are_illustrative: worked_example and anti_example captions demonstrate SHAPE ONLY. They are NOT factual claims and must never be reused as source material. Real captions must be built from game_state.json ground truth. Corrected 2026-09-04: nine worked examples still carried the caption shape from BEFORE the 2026-08-27 / 2026-09-01 render corrections -- five were simply short, and four (epic-handshake, eric-andre-shooting, is-this-a-pigeon, surprised-pikachu) had captions in the wrong boxes. Three valence rules had the same problem. uat/tests/test_meme_library.py now fails on any disagreement between valence, the examples, and boxes[].
_meta.box_count_convention: box_count is the template's TRUE physical caption count, taken from Imgflip's live get_memes API on 2026-08-27 (authoritative). Entries carrying box_count_source were corrected against it. Boxes flagged role_unverified have a correct COUNT but an inferred panel ORDER -- a single real render settles each. The 14 templates added 2026-09-15 took box_count from the same live API (meme_library_expand_probe.py) and had their panel ORDER confirmed by rendering marker captions and inspecting the image, so none carries role_unverified. flex-tape and mother-ignoring-kid-drowning were both non-obvious: flex-tape's index 2 is in the TOP panel, and the pool's index 2 is the mother rather than the drowning child.

Confirmed as inferred: left-exit-12-off-ramp, is-this-a-pigeon, buff-doge-vs-cheems, first-time, ight-imma-head-out. CORRECTED: eric-andre-shooting (subject box:2->box:0), trade-offer (subject box:0->box:2), epic-handshake (clasp is box 0, not box 2), surprised-pikachu (3 stacked caption lines, face uncaptioned), corporates-want-you-to-find-the-difference (box 2 is the observer; the verdict line is pre-printed), vince-mcmahon-reaction (box_count 4 -> 5; the old 4 shipped a blank payoff panel). spider-man-pointing-at-spider-man resolved 2026-09-01: exactly 2 boxes (top/bottom, centre-aligned, not on the figures). subject_abandons_sensible_for_funky.summary: A named subject faces an obviously correct option and visibly goes with the worse, pettier, or stranger one.
subject_abandons_sensible_for_funky.comedic_engine: The laugh is not the comparison -- it is that a real, named person actually chose the dumb thing while the audience can plainly see the right answer.
subject_abandons_sensible_for_funky.valence_rule: The abandoned option MUST be genuinely appealing or rational. The chosen option MUST be petty, self-defeating, or conspicuously odd. NEVER write the chosen option as the smarter one.
subject_abandons_sensible_for_funky.key_test: The choice is ALREADY MADE and public. We are reacting to it, not predicting it.
subject_abandons_sensible_for_funky.failure_mode: The straight upgrade: both options ranked with the second genuinely better. Produces an earnest endorsement or an ad, with zero comedy.

self_inflicted_realization.summary: The subject caused their own problem, and the reveal -- them realizing it, or conspicuously not -- is the punchline.
self_inflicted_realization.comedic_engine: Dramatic irony collapsing. The audience saw it coming; the subject is only now arriving, or is still pretending not to have arrived.
self_inflicted_realization.valence_rule: The damage MUST be traceable to the subject's own action. If an outside force caused it, this engine does not apply -- that is bad luck, not self-sabotage.
self_inflicted_realization.key_test: Could the subject have avoided this by not doing the thing they did? If no, wrong engine.
self_inflicted_realization.failure_mode: Blaming an external party. The moment someone else is at fault the joke evaporates.

never_arrives.summary: Something awaited -- an answer, a concession, an event -- never materializes, and the waiting itself becomes the joke.
never_arrives.comedic_engine: The gap between how reasonable the request is and how completely it goes unanswered. Repetition or decay stands in for the silence.
never_arrives.valence_rule: The awaited thing MUST be reasonable to want. If it is absurd to expect, the joke becomes mockery of the asker instead of the withholder.
never_arrives.key_test: Is the subject still waiting/asking as of today? If it already resolved, do not use this engine.
never_arrives.failure_mode: Using it for something that actually did arrive, which drains all the futility.

obliviousness_gap.summary: The subject's grasp of reality is comically out of step with what the audience can plainly see.
obliviousness_gap.comedic_engine: The audience is ahead of the subject. Either the subject is stunned by something inevitable, is only now noticing what was always true, or is confidently wrong.
obliviousness_gap.valence_rule: The truth MUST be genuinely obvious to the audience. If the audience is also surprised, there is no gap and nothing to laugh at.
obliviousness_gap.key_test: Would a casual fan have seen this coming? If not, the subject is not oblivious -- they are just informed.
obliviousness_gap.failure_mode: Applying it to a genuine surprise, which makes the subject look reasonable and the meme look mean.

escalating_ladder.summary: An ordered sequence of rungs, each more extreme than the last, ending somewhere absurd.
escalating_ladder.comedic_engine: The final rung. Rungs 1-3 build a credible pattern so the last one can break it -- either by going too far or by being ironically dumber than rung 1.
escalating_ladder.valence_rule: Rungs MUST escalate monotonically on ONE axis (sophistication, hype, absurdity). A rung that plateaus or reverses kills the build.
escalating_ladder.key_test: Are there genuinely FOUR distinct rungs? Two beats is a comparison -- use drake instead.
escalating_ladder.failure_mode: Four restatements of the same idea, which reads as padding rather than escalation.

denial_amid_disaster.summary: The subject presents calm or contentment while something is visibly going wrong.
denial_amid_disaster.comedic_engine: The gap between the composed face and the burning room. The insistence is what is funny, not the disaster.
denial_amid_disaster.valence_rule: The disaster MUST be real and visible, and the subject MUST be performing okayness about it. If they admit the problem, the engine collapses.
denial_amid_disaster.key_test: Is the subject claiming things are fine? If they are openly panicking, use a panic template instead.
denial_amid_disaster.failure_mode: Writing the subject as visibly upset, which removes the denial the whole template runs on.

contempt_face_off.summary: Two parties, one of them dismissive, mocking, or utterly unbothered by the other.
contempt_face_off.comedic_engine: The asymmetry of energy. One side is invested; the other cannot be bothered, and that imbalance is the joke.
contempt_face_off.valence_rule: The two sides MUST have mismatched energy -- one heated, one contemptuous or serene. Two equally angry parties is a fight, not this.
contempt_face_off.key_test: Is one side clearly not taking the other seriously?
contempt_face_off.failure_mode: Writing both sides at equal intensity, which flattens it into a generic argument.

awkward_exit_or_evasion.summary: The subject wants out of a situation -- either glancing away guiltily or actually leaving.
awkward_exit_or_evasion.comedic_engine: The physical comedy of retreat. The subject has decided this is not their problem and is visibly withdrawing.
awkward_exit_or_evasion.valence_rule: The situation MUST be one the subject has some stake in. Withdrawing from something irrelevant is not funny -- the stake is what makes the exit cowardly.
awkward_exit_or_evasion.key_test: Does the subject have a reason to stay? If not, leaving is just sensible.
awkward_exit_or_evasion.failure_mode: No implicated subject, leaving the exit unmotivated.

they_are_the_same.summary: Two things presented or behaving as distinct turn out to be functionally identical.
they_are_the_same.comedic_engine: The reveal of hidden sameness -- either a false distinction being sold, or two rivals who are mirror images while accusing each other.
they_are_the_same.valence_rule: The two things MUST be genuinely equivalent in the way that matters. If a real difference exists, the joke is simply wrong.
they_are_the_same.key_test: Could you swap the two and have nothing meaningfully change?
they_are_the_same.failure_mode: Forcing sameness onto things that are actually different, which reads as a bad take rather than a joke.

hardened_vs_soft.summary: A lopsided contrast between a hardened, battle-worn party and a soft, shocked, or diminished one.
hardened_vs_soft.comedic_engine: The veteran's indifference. What devastates one side is routine to the other, and that asymmetry of suffering is the joke.
hardened_vs_soft.valence_rule: The hardened side MUST be unimpressed BECAUSE of accumulated experience. If they are unimpressed for no reason, it is just rudeness.
hardened_vs_soft.key_test: Has the hardened side plainly been through worse?
hardened_vs_soft.failure_mode: Two parties with equivalent experience, which erases the gap the template needs.

forced_choice_dilemma.summary: A subject frozen between two options of the SAME valence -- both appealing, or both painful -- that cannot coexist.
forced_choice_dilemma.comedic_engine: The paralysis is the joke, not the options. Either the audience finds the answer obvious and the subject clearly does not, or the two buttons expose a hypocrisy the subject created themselves.
forced_choice_dilemma.valence_rule: The two options MUST be same-valence and genuinely in conflict. If one is clearly better there is no sweat and the meme dies.
forced_choice_dilemma.key_test: The choice is NOT yet made -- the subject is still sweating. If it is made, use subject_abandons_sensible_for_funky.
forced_choice_dilemma.failure_mode: Writing it as a ranked preference, which is the abandons-sensible engine wearing the wrong template.

lopsided_exchange.summary: A transaction framed as mutual that is transparently one-sided.
lopsided_exchange.comedic_engine: The formal, polite framing of a robbery. The deal-making language is what sells it.
lopsided_exchange.valence_rule: What the proposer gets MUST clearly outweigh what they give. A fair trade has no joke in it.
lopsided_exchange.key_test: Would anyone actually accept this deal?
lopsided_exchange.failure_mode: Writing a balanced trade, which is just a transaction description.

understated_difficulty.summary: Solemnly correcting the assumption that something is easy.
understated_difficulty.comedic_engine: Epic gravitas applied to the mundane. The weight of the delivery against the ordinariness of the task.
understated_difficulty.valence_rule: The task MUST be widely assumed easy AND actually be hard. If everyone already knows it is hard, there is nothing to correct.
understated_difficulty.failure_mode: Applying it to something obviously difficult, which makes the gravitas redundant.

unexpected_common_ground.summary: Two normally-opposed parties turn out to share one thing.
unexpected_common_ground.comedic_engine: The unlikely alliance. Two camps that agree on nothing are caught agreeing on this.
unexpected_common_ground.valence_rule: The two parties MUST be genuinely opposed, and the shared thing MUST be specific. Vague common ground is not a joke.
unexpected_common_ground.failure_mode: Two allied parties agreeing, which is unremarkable.

emotional_whiplash.summary: A three-beat swing: worry, relief, then a worse worry that cancels the relief.
emotional_whiplash.comedic_engine: The rug-pull in beat three. Beat two has to genuinely reassure or the reversal has nothing to undo.
emotional_whiplash.valence_rule: Beat 1 negative, beat 2 genuinely reassuring, beat 3 worse than beat 1. All three beats MUST be about the same thread.
emotional_whiplash.key_test: Does the middle beat actually provide relief?
emotional_whiplash.failure_mode: Three escalating negatives with no relief beat, which is just a list of bad news.

provocative_dare.summary: Planting a contestable opinion and inviting argument.
provocative_dare.comedic_engine: The confrontational calm. The subject stakes out a spicy position and sits there waiting.
provocative_dare.valence_rule: The take MUST be genuinely debatable -- something a reasonable fan would argue with. A consensus opinion has no dare in it.
provocative_dare.key_test: Would this actually start an argument?
provocative_dare.failure_mode: Stating something uncontroversial, which makes the dare limp.

simple_take_vindicated.summary: Three readings of one question: the blunt take, the over-thought take, and the blunt take again -- vindicated.
simple_take_vindicated.comedic_engine: The two ends agree and only the middle is working hard. The analysis is the butt of the joke, not the answer.
simple_take_vindicated.valence_rule: The two ends MUST land on the SAME conclusion, close to word-for-word. The middle MUST be more sophisticated AND more wrong.
simple_take_vindicated.key_test: Is the simple take actually correct? If the analysis is right and the simple take is wrong, this engine inverts and dies.
simple_take_vindicated.failure_mode: Three different takes with no repeat, which is a list of opinions rather than a curve.

mismatched_response.summary: The response is wildly out of proportion to the problem -- a trivial patch on a catastrophe, or attention lavished on the wrong thing while the real one drowns.
mismatched_response.comedic_engine: The subject is visibly doing something, which is what makes it worse than doing nothing. Effort aimed at the wrong target.
mismatched_response.valence_rule: The problem MUST be real and large, and the response MUST be plainly too small or aimed elsewhere. If the response would actually work, there is no joke.
mismatched_response.key_test: Would a neutral observer say the response is proportionate? If yes, wrong engine.
mismatched_response.failure_mode: Writing a fix that is merely imperfect rather than absurdly undersized, which reads as ordinary criticism.

outside_looking_in.summary: One event, two seats: someone is inside it and someone is shut out or stuck with the worse view.
outside_looking_in.comedic_engine: The gap between the two seats, not the event. The excluded party knowing exactly what they are missing is what stings.
outside_looking_in.valence_rule: Both sides MUST be looking at the SAME thing. The shut-out side MUST have had a credible claim to be inside it, or the exclusion is unremarkable.
outside_looking_in.key_test: Would the shut-out party reasonably have expected to be in it?
outside_looking_in.failure_mode: Two unrelated situations placed side by side, which is a comparison rather than an exclusion.

truth_refused.summary: The subject is handed a plain, accurate answer and will not take it -- either discarding it outright or building something elaborate in its place.
truth_refused.comedic_engine: The effort spent avoiding a one-sentence truth. The work of the avoidance is funnier than the truth itself.
truth_refused.valence_rule: The refused truth MUST be accurate and plainly stated. If it is an insult rather than a fact, the meme punches instead of landing.
truth_refused.key_test: Is there a simple true answer the subject is visibly stepping around?
truth_refused.failure_mode: Writing the 'truth' as an opinion, which turns the refusal into a reasonable disagreement.

obligatory_ritual.summary: A thing said or done every single year, on cue, by someone visibly tired of saying it.
obligatory_ritual.comedic_engine: The weariness of the performer against the undimmed delight of the crowd. Everyone knows the line is coming and it works anyway.
obligatory_ritual.valence_rule: The line MUST be genuinely recurring -- an annual or seasonal fixture the audience can recite. A one-off statement has no ritual in it.
obligatory_ritual.key_test: Has this happened in at least two prior seasons?
obligatory_ritual.failure_mode: Using it for a first-time event, which leaves the crowd nothing to be anticipating.
